clue.text: Mail to open, in a flurry? Do it later!

parts.note: mail is the post, the letters delivered

indicators.note: a flurry is a commotion, so the letters of the word open are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flustered by the post tells themselves to put off opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like the thing being opened, but it supplies the first piece; 'in a flurry' scrambles the word open, and 'to' merely attaches it.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer something is to put it off, and the imperative 'Do it later!' is that command.

clue.text: Parking, fix immovably by hedge

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
to rivet is to fasten firmly with metal pins

explanation.surface: A car is parked and bolted firmly beside a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is a shrub widely grown as garden hedging.

clue.text: Almost the only approach to Scottish firth

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: sole means the only one
a way is a route or means of approach

explanation.surface: Nearly the only way in to an estuary in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the word for 'the only'. The Solway Firth is the estuary on the border between south-west Scotland and Cumbria in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solway Firth is the estuary on the border between south-west Scotland and England.

clue.text: They're made for a pound

parts.note: reads as cheap goods sold for one pound sterling, but pound is the verb, to crush with a mortar

explanation.surface: Items on sale at a bargain price of a pound each.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestles are tools designed for grinding and crushing in a mortar.

clue.text: Lighting, indicating direction ahead?

parts.note: NE, northeast, is a compass direction
on means forward or ahead

explanation.surface: A lit sign points the way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: NE is a compass direction and ON means ahead, as in 'go on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is the gas used in glowing tube signs, so it stands for a form of lighting.

clue.text: About time French artist's retrospective put on show

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other here
looking back, so the painter's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: A retrospective of a French painter's work is finally being put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns DEGAS into SAGED, and 'About' puts that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged has been mounted and presented to an audience.

clue.text: Turning red, don't get stamped upon!

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flushing red begs not to be trampled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges REDDONT (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Something trodden has been walked or stepped on, a synonym.

clue.text: Princely ruse gone awry

indicators.note: something gone awry is out of place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prince's trick has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awry' rearranges RUSEGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Princely means lavish or handsome, as a generous sum or gift is.

clue.text: Identify sad ego in disturbed characters

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist picks out a sad ego in disturbed individuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed characters' says the letters of SADEGOIN are rearranged; 'characters' means letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify an illness or problem from its symptoms.

clue.text: Sun oil I'll for the most part reapply? Not true!

indicators.note: applying the letters again in a fresh arrangement signals a rearrangement
most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: I'll written without its apostrophe gives these three letters

explanation.surface: A sunbather wonders whether to put on more sun oil, but the protection is a myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts ILL to IL; 'reapply' rearranges SUNOIL plus IL. The definition is an exclamation: an illusion is something not true, so the noun answers the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A delusion or false impression is something that is not true, which the exclamation flags.

clue.text: Eye part of the maize cob, you'll hear

indicators.note: what a listener hears points to a word that sounds like another

parts.note: an ear of corn is the cob of maize, so the phrase gives two words

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to ask about part of a corn cob.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'corn ear' runs together into the name of the eye's transparent front layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent dome covering the iris and pupil is a component of the eyeball.

clue.text: Discussion about second herb

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a parley is a discussion, especially between opponents

explanation.surface: A conversation about a second herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PARLEY round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common culinary herb.

clue.text: Facilitate moving west from Mediterranean island to new England

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftwards, so the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's first exile

explanation.surface: Someone helps another relocate from a Mediterranean island to New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new England' looks like the US region, but it is two abbreviations, N and E; in an across answer 'moving west' means read leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To facilitate something is to make it possible or easier, a synonym.

clue.text: Person with almost enough audacity to become a bureaucrat

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: nearly the full amount, so the word for audacity loses its last letter

parts.note: audacity is daring, boldness

explanation.surface: A man with nearly enough nerve might rise to be a senior official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost enough' reads as part of the surface's story about nerve, but it is the signal to drop the final letter of the word for audacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful senior civil servant, originally an official of imperial China.

clue.text: Roofing material worker put in a heap

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a pile is a heap
a worker is a worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A labourer puts roofing material in a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the crossword's usual ant (a worker ant), and 'put in' signals that it goes inside the heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantile is a curved S-shaped roof tile.

clue.text: Bloodsuckers latching on to a couple of donkeys — awfully big 'uns

indicators.note: two copies of the word for one donkey are put side by side

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bloodsucking insects fasten on to two donkeys, and they are horribly large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' doubles ASS; 'awfully' rearranges BIGUNS into INBUGS. Assassin bugs are predatory insects, some of which suck blood.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects of the family Reduviidae pierce their prey and feed on its blood or body fluids.

clue.text: One acted badly, now it's told

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone performed poorly and the story is now being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ONEACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing story told about a real incident.

clue.text: Glasses for gymnasts

explanation.surface: Drinking glasses provided for gymnasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers are flat-bottomed drinking vessels, and also acrobats who perform somersaults.

clue.text: Eurasian then breaks dn in stress condition

indicators.note: dn is the abbreviation for down, so 'breaks down' signals the words are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone of mixed Asian and European heritage collapses under a stress-related illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks dn' (dn is short for down) rearranges the twelve letters of EURASIANTHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurasthenia is an old diagnosis of nervous exhaustion, often attributed to overwork and strain.

clue.text: Flier taking a route over rocky height?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over (above) the next

parts.note: via, Latin for way, means by a route through
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A pilot flies a route over a rocky peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a leaflet or a bird, but it is a pilot; 'over' works because in a down answer the earlier pieces sit above the later ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Sounds a popular place for gaining perspicacity

indicators.note: sounds signals that the spoken form of one phrase gives another word

parts.note: in means popular, and a site is a place

explanation.surface: A fashionable spot is said to sharpen one's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: IN (popular) plus SITE (place) is said aloud the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacity is keen understanding, as is insight.

clue.text: Old boy her majesty takes on as king

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A former pupil is taken on by the Queen as king.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, ER and ON in a row; Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Gets away from ducks, perhaps?

explanation.surface: Something escapes from some ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like the birds, but it is the verb to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape from something, and ducking a blow or question is one way of evading it.

clue.text: Type of furniture leg dancers leap

explanation.surface: Something about chair legs and ballet jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved, S-shaped chair leg bears this name, as does a ballet jump in which one leg beats against the other in the air.

clue.text: Girl lives with boy

parts.note: to live is to exist, so lives gives is
Abel is a boy's name, the son of Adam in Genesis

explanation.surface: A girl moves in with her boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female given name.

clue.text: Root to eat with salt and nothing more

parts.note: a salt or tar is a sailor
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A root vegetable eaten with just salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like seasoning but means a sailor, TAR. Taro is a starchy tropical root.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a starchy tuber grown in the tropics and cooked as a staple food.

clue.text: The first note from poetic song to her

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, often meant to be sung

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word The is taken

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A poem addressed to a woman, starting with its first note.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare pronoun: the heroine of Swan Lake, to whom the 'poetic song' is addressed. ODE is followed by T, the first of 'The', and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is a woman's name, best known as the swan princess in Tchaikovsky's ballet.

clue.text: Harassed by ruinous, unrestrained greed

parts.note: something ruinous is bad

indicators.note: letters not held in place are free to scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was pestered by destructive, unchecked greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruinous' seems to describe the greed, but it supplies its own piece; 'unrestrained' then lets the letters of greed run loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or nag them persistently.

clue.text: Warrant to proceed right inside

indicators.note: one piece placed within the other

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on or proceed

explanation.surface: A legal warrant lets someone proceed, with justice on their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R within ENSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to guarantee it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Satisfies the constituents

explanation.surface: A politician pleases the voters in their district.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is pleases (a verb); the other is the items or ingredients that make up something (a plural noun).
